notes.meaning: The group of prophets in training told Elisha that their meeting place was becoming much too small. Under Elisha's teaching, more and more students had joined the community. Even in a time when many in the nation turned from God, faithful believers still gathered to learn His word.

The students asked Elisha for permission to cut logs near the Jordan River to build a larger place to live, and Elisha told them to go. The banks of the Jordan had plenty of timber for simple buildings. These men were humble and willing to work hard with their own hands.

One of the students asked Elisha to come along with them, and Elisha agreed to go. The students deeply respected their teacher and wanted his presence, advice, and blessing while they worked. It is good to seek godly guidance in our daily projects.

Elisha went with them to the Jordan, and the men began chopping down trees. The prophet was willing to join his students in their ordinary manual labor. Together, they worked to meet the needs of their growing group.

While one student was cutting a log, the iron head of his axe flew off and sank into deep water. He cried out in distress to Elisha because the axe was borrowed. Iron tools were valuable, and as a poor man he had no money to replace it.

Elisha asked where it had fallen, cut a stick, threw it into the water, and made the heavy iron float to the top. The stick had no natural power to lift heavy metal, but God used it as a sign of His supernatural power. The Lord cares about His people even in their small, everyday worries.

Elisha told the man to pick up the axe head, and the student reached out his hand and took it. God worked the miracle that no man could do, but He still asked the man to take action himself. We must gladly receive what God provides.

The king of Aram went to war against Israel and planned secret ambushes with his officers. He wanted to catch the Israelite army by surprise instead of fighting an open battle. God's enemies often make clever plans, but nothing is hidden from God.

Elisha sent a warning to the king of Israel not to go near that place because the enemy was waiting there. God revealed the secret ambush to His prophet to save the nation from harm. Even though the king was not faithful, God showed great mercy to Israel.

The king of Israel checked the place Elisha warned him about and stationed guards there, keeping himself safe several times. God faithfully warned the king about physical danger through the prophet. Sadly, people often listen to warnings about earthly danger while ignoring warnings about their sins.

The king of Aram was furious because all his surprise attacks were failing. He called his officers together and demanded to know who among them was secretly working for Israel. He assumed there had to be a traitor inside his own royal court.

One of his servants explained that no one in the court was a spy. Instead, Elisha the prophet was telling the king of Israel the very words spoken in the Aramean king's private bedroom. God knows every secret word and thought, and no human plan can be hidden from Him.

The king ordered his men to find out where Elisha was staying so he could capture him, and they reported that he was in Dothan. Dothan was a town on a hill about twelve miles north of Samaria. The king foolishly thought he could surprise a man who knew his secret thoughts.

The king of Aram sent a massive army with horses and chariots to surround Dothan by night. He used a huge military force against just one prophet. Those who fight against God often rely on great earthly power, forgetting that no army can defeat the Lord.

Elisha's servant got up early, went outside, and saw the entire city surrounded by enemy troops and chariots. Paralyzed with fear, he ran to Elisha and cried out, asking what they could do. He looked only at the physical danger and felt totally trapped.

Elisha told his servant not to be afraid because those on their side outnumbered the enemy. The prophet knew that God and His heavenly host were there to protect them. God's people do not need to panic when they remember how great the Lord's power is.

Elisha prayed for the Lord to open the young man's eyes, and he suddenly saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha. These fiery chariots were God's unseen angels guarding the prophet. Faith does not invent unreal things; it sees the real protection God has already provided.

As the Aramean soldiers marched toward him, Elisha prayed for God to strike them with blindness, and the Lord did. This was a mental confusion where they could still walk, but could no longer recognize who they were seeing. God has full control over the human mind and protects His servants as He pleases.

Elisha told the confused soldiers that they were on the wrong road and offered to lead them to the man they wanted. He then guided the entire enemy force straight into the capital city of Samaria. This clever war stratagem disarmed the enemy without any bloodshed.

Once they were inside Samaria, Elisha asked God to open their eyes, and the soldiers were shocked to find themselves inside Israel's fortified capital. Their confusion vanished, and they realized they were totally trapped. God easily turns the schemes of His enemies upside down.

When the king of Israel saw the trapped soldiers, he eagerly asked Elisha twice if he should kill them. The king spoke politely by calling Elisha his father, but he was eager to slaughter them. He waited for the prophet's word before doing anything.

Elisha ordered the king not to kill them, reminding him that even regular war prisoners were not put to death in cold blood. Instead, he commanded the king to give them bread and water and send them home to their master. God called His people to show mercy and overcome evil with good.

The king prepared a huge feast for the Aramean troops, fed them, and sent them back to their master. Because of this mercy and the great power they witnessed, the raiding bands stopped attacking the land of Israel for a time. Treating enemies with kindness can win a far greater victory than weapons.

Some time later, King Ben-hadad of Aram gathered his whole army and laid siege to Samaria. The earlier feast had stopped the small border raids, but it did not change the greedy heart of the Aramean king. His army surrounded the city to starve its people into giving up.

The siege lasted so long that severe starvation hit Samaria, and food prices rose out of control. Even a donkey's head, an unclean animal with barely any meat, cost eighty pieces of silver, and a handful of coarse seeds, called dove's dung, cost five pieces of silver. The terrible prices showed how desperate life had become inside the city walls.

As the king of Israel walked along the city wall to check the defenses, a desperate woman cried out to him for help. In times of extreme trouble, citizens turned to their ruler for justice and protection. She hoped her king could do something to relieve her misery.

The king replied that if the Lord would not help her, he had no grain from the floor or wine from the press to give. He acknowledged that human rulers are powerless when God withholds His blessing. Without God's help, earthly leaders have nothing to offer.

When the king asked what was wrong, the woman told him that she and another mother had agreed to cook and eat their own children to survive. After they ate her son, the other woman hid her child to save him. This dreadful tragedy fulfilled God's ancient warning about the horrors Israel would suffer if they turned away from Him.

Hearing the woman's awful story, the king tore his clothes in grief and shock. As he walked along the wall, the people saw that he was wearing rough sackcloth against his skin as an outward sign of mourning. He felt the pain of the crisis deeply, but his heart was still not truly humble before God.

The king flew into a rage and swore an oath to have Elisha's head cut off before the day was done. Instead of repenting of his own sins, he blamed God's prophet for the disaster. Unbelieving leaders often lash out at God's servants rather than facing their own guilt.

Elisha was sitting at home with the city elders when God showed him that an executioner was on the way. He called the king the son of a murderer, pointing back to wicked King Ahab, and told the elders to hold the door shut against the messenger. Elisha delayed the killer because he knew the king was hurrying right behind him.

While Elisha was speaking, the messenger and the king arrived, and the king declared in despair that this disaster came from the Lord. He asked why he should wait for God's help any longer. He knew God was in control of the affliction, but he gave in to anger and hopelessness instead of trusting the Lord.
